title: The Hidden Reason Judas Followed Jesus
paragraphs:
The Hidden Reason Judas Followed Jesus
John 12:6
He kissed the door of heaven… and still loved money more.
That’s the terror of Judas.

John does not leave us guessing.
“He was a thief.”
Not confused.
Not merely disappointed.
Not just “misunderstood.”
He was close to Jesus in body, but far from Him in heart.

Judas followed Christ while secretly serving another god.
Not Baal.
Not Rome.
Mammon.

He liked the ministry bag more than the Master.
He stayed near the miracles, near the anointing, near the power, near the bread multiplying, near the dead rising—but his heart kept reaching for silver.
And that’s where this gets painfully personal.

You can walk with Jesus publicly and still worship something else privately.
You can hold the money bag and still lose your soul.
You can preach, post, sing, serve, and still have a heart that has never fully bowed.
But here’s what we miss:

Judas did not betray Jesus in one night.
He betrayed Him little by little.
A tolerated greed.
A secret theft.
A divided loyalty.
A heart that never truly repented.

That is how many souls fall.
Not all at once.
By inches.

John 12:6 exposes more than Judas.
It exposes every false disciple who wants Jesus for access, influence, provision, or image—but not for lordship.
And yet, even here, grace is speaking.

Because the warning of Judas is not written to entertain us.
It is written to wake us up.

If there is hidden greed in you, bring it to Christ.
If there is divided love in you, bring it to Christ.
If you have been using Jesus instead of surrendering to Him, bring that too.

The Gospel is not that Judas was bad and Peter was good.
The Gospel is that sinners can still be washed by the blood of Jesus when they truly repent and run to Him.
Peter wept and returned.
Judas hid and hardened.
So choose today.

Not silver.
Not image.
Not secret sin.
Choose Christ.

Because Jesus does not just expose false worship.
He offers mercy to all who repent.
